title: The Bible and Its Interpreters
description: The Bible is one of the most widely read books of all time, the contents of which have generated countless different interpretations over the centuries. In doing so, we will focus on the major themes and figures of the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament and New Testament.

description: Reads classical texts that expound the fundamental mythological stories and elements of the Western tradition, then will read selected texts from the Renaissance through the twentieth century that utilize these myths. title: Roman Drama
description: Latin literature begins in 240 BCE, when Livius Andronicus produced a comedy and a tragedy translated from Greek at the Ludi Romani that year. Early Roman comedy is represented primarily by the twenty (nearly complete) extant plays of Titus Maccius Plautus (254-184 BCE) and the six surviving plays of Publius Terentius Afer (fl. 160s BCE). Early Roman tragedy survives only in the fragments of such playwrights as Gnaeus Naevius (280-201 BCE), Quintus Ennius (239-169 BCE), Marcus Pacuvius (220-130) and Lucius Accius (170-86 BCE). We are also fortunate to possess eight tragedies of Lucius Annaeus Seneca or “Seneca the Younger” (1 BCE-65 CE). This course will provide a survey of Roman drama, both comic and tragic, with a special focus on three plays: Plautus’ Pseudolus , Terence’s Hecyra , and Seneca’s Thyestes .
